digest.key_takeaway: Google has released Android Bench 2.0, a major update to its benchmark framework for evaluating AI models and agents on Android development tasks. The update introduces long-horizon tasks (LHTs), agent-based evaluation, and continuous scoring to better assess performance on complex, multi-step development tasks. By Sergio De Simone

articles.title: The Farmers Market Gig: Prices, Crowds, and What's Actually in Season
articles.summary:
Every Saturday, the same farmers market looks completely different. Heirloom tomatoes at $4 a pound last week, gone today. First apples of the season, handwritten sign, no price anywhere online. Markets don't update a database — they chalk a board and sell until they run out. So the simplest job appears: go there, look, report back.

articles.title: The Break-Room Gig: Five Micro-Tasks You Can Do Without Leaving Your Work Block
articles.summary:
Most gig work asks you to drive across town. A new kind asks you to just walk downstairs. AI agents are bad at knowing what is happening on your block right now: Is the café line spilling onto the sidewalk? Is the pharmacy actually open? That gap is why agents pay people for tiny, local checks — five to ten minutes, one photo or one clear answer.

articles.title: The Agent Workforce Stack: Identity, Briefing, Dispatch, Proof, Payment
articles.summary:
When an AI agent hires a human to do something in the physical world, it looks simple from the outside. The agent posts a task. A person nearby does it. Money moves.

In practice, five separate systems have to work in sequence, and each can fail in its own way. Call it the agent workforce stack: identity, briefing, dispatch, proof, and payment. If you are building agents that need hands, eyes, or presence, this is the stack you are actually building.

articles.title: Is UAT testing difficult for business teams?
articles.summary:
UAT testing is not difficult when your operational team tests against clear, measurable criteria agreed before engineering begins. User acceptance testing is where you verify the software meets the agreed requirements against documented criteria, and sign it off before launch. Because your business team validates familiar workflows using realistic records rather than inspecting code, the entire review process stays predictable, structured and straightforward for everyone involved.

articles.title: Github Migrates Copilot Runtime to Rust with AI-Assisted Rewrite
articles.summary: GitHub migrated more than 800,000 lines of Copilot runtime code from TypeScript and Node.js to Rust in about 14.5 weeks using AI-assisted development. The incremental migration used N-API interoperability, automated testing, human review, and 128 pull requests while continuing to ship releases. By Leela Kumili

articles.title: HashiCorp Relased Terraform Google Cloud Provider 8.0 in General Availability
articles.summary: HashiCorp has announced the general availability of version 8.0 of the Terraform provider for Google Cloud. The major release updates the default load balancing for two Compute Engine resources. It also removes resources linked to retired Google Cloud services. By Claudio Masolo

articles.title: Olson and Söderqvist Discuss Valkey’s Evolution and Future Past Caching Use Cases at OSS EU
articles.summary: Valkey is a growing project, launched as a fork of Redis over two years ago, supported by twelve maintainers and nine committee members from various companies. Recent developments include enhanced throughput, improved cluster functionality, and plans for features like synchronous replication and tiered storage. The project also emphasises security and release efficiency through automation. By Olimpiu Pop

articles.title: Cloudflare K2 Builds Event Streams on R2 Object Storage, at a Second of Produce Latency
articles.summary: Cloudflare has launched K2 in public beta, a serverless event streaming service implementing a durable log on R2 object storage. Cloudflare states produce latency of about one second at p99; a tester reported end-to-end p99 of 7.5 seconds, which a commenter answering for the team said was higher than expected. Consume charges match produce charges per GB. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
